Assistant: The sweep is now doing exactly what you wanted — finding real breakage and fixing it. Concrete progress this cycle:

**Real bugs found (content rendering is genuinely broken):** Batch 3 (Sonnet) did honest work — 31 screenshots, 5 PASS / 5 FAIL — and filed 6 real defects: links not tappable (#62), video shows "unavailable" (#63), hashtags plain text not chips (#64), quoted notes show a raw stub (#65), NIP-23 articles show a raw URL (#66), and the feed exposes **zero accessibility elements** so VoiceOver is broken (#67).

**Already fixing them:** launched a render-fix agent on a dedicated sim to fix all 6 properly (no hacks — real tappable links, hashtag chips, resolved quote/article cards, accessibility identifiers) and **reverify each with an after-screenshot** before closing. That's the file→fix→reverify loop you required.

**Two orchestration lessons I acted on:**
- Running 3 sim testers concurrently is unsafe — they collide on the shared xcode MCP session profile (Batch 3 caught its profile getting hijacked mid-run). I'm **serializing** the remaining sim testers and having every agent re-assert its sim UDID per call.
- I under-seeded the relay (4 of 8 content types); Batch 3 self-corrected by publishing the rest. Fixtures are richer now.

**Where the 70 scenarios stand:** real evidence for S01–S10, S18–S27, S28–S36; S11–S17 and S37–S40/S62–S64 finishing now (I'll scrutinize those two for collision damage since they ran concurrently). Remaining: DMs, Groups, Wallet/Relays/Diagnostics, Offline (SIM-only), cross-cutting UI.

The 30-min heartbeat is holding me to real evidence, not "agents running." I'll report as the render fixes reverify and the remaining batches land — and nothing gets called done until the Opus review reads every screenshot and everything imperfect is fixed and reverified.
